correctness.rationale: For N=x+y+z, alpha+beta=2 gives the exact logistic identity Ndot=N(1-N). Compact support inside the positive octant makes log N and one-coordinate logarithmic antiderivative tests legitimate. Invariance of log N and N yields E[N]=E[N^2]=1, hence N=1 almost surely. Testing H'(x)=phi(x)/x gives E[alpha y+beta z|x]=1-x; together with y+z=1-x and alpha!=1 this forces E[y|x]=E[z|x]=(1-x)/2, cyclically. The global means are 1/3. On the simplex the per-capita speeds reduce pointwise to (alpha-1) times pairwise differences, and the identity sum_{pairs}(x-y)^2=3 sum x^2-(x+y+z)^2 gives exactly the displayed factor 3 multiplying the sum of variances.
risks: Compact positive support is essential for the logarithmic tests; boundary heteroclinic measures are outside scope.
